bibliographic_scope.title: Self-Organization of Ordered Silver Nanocrystal Arrays on Cubic Mesoporous Silica Surfaces
bibliographic_scope.authors: Lian-Zhou Wang; Jian-Lin Shi; Wen-Hua Zhang; Mei-Ling Ruan; Jian Yu; Dong-Sheng Yan

source_interpretation.text: The authors propose that capillary filling introduces AgNO3/ethanol into silica mesochannels; evaporation leaves adsorbed silver and nitrate species. The AS complex remains tentative.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Impregnation and adsorption discussion

source_interpretation.text: The source interprets 300 °C treatment as nitrate decomposition and formation/redistribution of Ag clusters. A periodic surface stress field is proposed to influence array organization; the intrinsic driving force remains unresolved.

Ag line width/gaps/periodicity and silica mesoporosity are distinct length scales. Larger particles after 500 °C and beam-stable square arrays are source observations, not a continuous predictive growth model.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 3–4 and 500 °C follow-up

sample_lineage.AS: PS degassed, impregnated with AgNO3/ethanol and room-temperature dried.
sample_lineage.AST: An unspecified part of AS heated at 300 °C for 2 h.
sample_lineage.AST_500C: Incomplete follow-up on AST; arrays absent and larger particles observed, no exact duration.

characterization.XRD: Rigaku D/Max-series instrument; printed model suffix is unresolved. Cu Kα radiation. Low-angle 2θ = 2–10° MCM-48 features and high-angle 10–80° Ag comparison.
characterization.microscopy: JEOL-200 CX; source states 200 keV. Figures 2 and 3 SAD along [110] of the mesostructure; Figure 4 room-temperature beam exposure partly damages silica while Ag arrays persist.
characterization.nitrogen: Micromeritics ASAP 2400, 77 K. BET linear range P/P0 = 0.05–0.15; BJH for pore metrics.
characterization.isotherms: PS and AST: type IV; sharp step P/P0 = 0.2–0.3 and H3 hysteresis P/P0 = 0.4–1. Numerical isotherm curves are not supplied.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Characterization and Figures1–4/Table1

source_interpretation_limits: Capillary adsorption, surface hydroxyl/dangling bond complexing, stress-field-directed cluster assembly and thermal mobility are attributed proposals. No energy-barrier measurement, Ag loading percentage or independent complex structure is supplied.

limitations: Complete supplied three-page main, Figures 1–4, Table 1 and all 23 references. SI and cited full sources unreviewed.

Silica precursor amounts are given as a gel molar composition, not absolute charges. Starting CTAB/NaOH solution concentrations, mixing order, gel temperature, autoclave capacity, wash volumes and 60 °C drying duration are unreported.

Numerical vacuum, cooling duration, impregnation addition rate and room-temperature drying time are unreported. Three milliliters is the AgNO3/ethanol solution charge, not a separately quantified ethanol volume.
Only part of AS received the 300 °C treatment; the amount, heating ramp and atmosphere are not given. The 500 °C follow-up duration, ramp, atmosphere and exact specimen fraction are unknown.

PS, AS and AST are source-labelled successive states, not independently reproduced batches. Cross-record lineage links retain their source scope without copying parent products or inventing repeated preparations.

Cubic MCM-48 order and [110] directions refer to mesoporous structure. Ag array width, gap and line spacing are not atomic Ag unit-cell parameters. No measured atomic or finite-particle coordinates are supplied.

The silver-ion/nitrate complex in AS is tentative, not a resolved molecular structure. The source does not quantify the Ag content, size distribution, array fraction or larger-particle dimensions after 500 °C.
No optical, electronic, catalytic or adsorption-capacity application experiment is supplied beyond the reported nitrogen pore characterization. Proposed assembly forces remain interpretation.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending.
